proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Put \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\).  For \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\), define the profiled finite risk and its mixed-pair mean by
\[
 \mathscr V_J(q)=\min_{\eta}\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s_J}}
 \mathcal R_h(q,\eta),
 \qquad
 \bar m(q)=\int_{\Delta_2}m(x)\,d\mu_q(x).
\]
On the common space \(\mathcal P(\Delta_2)\), define the extended-real residual functional
\[
 \mathscr G_J(\mu)=
 \inf_{\substack{q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\\ \mu_q=\mu}}
 J^{4/3}\!\left\{\mathscr V_J(q)-\frac{1}{2J}\right\},
\]
where the infimum over an empty set is \(+\infty\).  The second-order pair-orbit selection problem is to derive, from the ten pair types, the kernel \(K\), and the local fluctuations of \(\tau\), an equicoercive epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit for \((\mathscr G_J)\), including all boundary tangent cones induced by the hard constraints.

When \(\rho=1/2\) and \(\kappa_J\to\kappa\in\mathbb R\), the candidate limit on the first-order face is
\[
 \mathscr G_\kappa(\mu)=
 \begin{cases}
 \mathscr A(\mu)+\kappa\!\left(2\displaystyle\int m\,d\mu-1\right),
   & \mu\in\mathcal F_{1/2},\\
 +\infty, & \mu\notin\mathcal F_{1/2},
 \end{cases}
\]
where \(\mathscr A\) is the unrestricted Airy/local-experiment correction.  The hard-budget summand has the required scale because
\[
 J^{4/3}\frac{\{2\bar m(q)-1\}\Delta_J}{J^2}
 =\kappa_J\{2\bar m(q)-1\}.
\]
The displayed candidate is recorded only as upper-bound evidence: neither a matching lower expansion nor epi- or \(\Gamma\)-convergence is built into this definition.

The singular regimes are separate problems.  If \(\kappa_J\to+\infty\), bounded candidate residual on \(\mathcal F_{1/2}\), where \(\int m\,d\mu\ge1/2\), forces \(\int m\,d\mu=1/2\) before the \(\mathscr A\)-contact problem is considered.  If \(\kappa_J\to-\infty\), recentering by \(\kappa_J\) changes the hard-budget term to
\[
 2|\kappa_J|\!\left(1-\int m\,d\mu\right),
\]
so bounded recentered candidate residual forces \(\int m\,d\mu=1\), hence \(\mu=\delta_{(0,0,1)}\) on \(\mathcal F_{1/2}\), before any next-order tie-breaker.  When \(\rho>1/2\), the hard budget is macroscopically separated from the critical boundary; one must derive a distinct unrestricted local-experiment limit restricted to \(\mathcal F_\rho\), rather than infer it by declaring \(\kappa=+\infty\).  A contact-set description of \(\mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\) is valid only after matching liminf and recovery bounds and compactness for exact finite minimizers have been proved.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The old handle named no scaling, residual functional, or contact problem. The corrected construction defines \(\Delta_J\), \(\kappa_J\), the profiled residual risk, the candidate finite-\(\kappa\) functional, and the distinct infinite-\(\kappa\) and \(\rho>1/2\) regimes while explicitly withholding an unproved matching lower expansion.

proposed.comparator_claim: Given an assignment vector and an invariant estimator, uniform randomization over the permutation group is minimax under invariant states and a quasiconvex objective.
The mixed-strategy optimal design minimizes worst-case variance of difference in means over a structured conditional-mean class and may require randomization over several partitions.
For unrestricted binary potential outcomes, Bernoulli assignment with a nonlinear posterior-mean rule attains the all-procedure minimax risk, whose second-order term is governed by the Airy function.

For unrestricted bounded-interval potential outcomes, independent assignment with a nonlinear estimator is minimax; the present unrestricted binary endpoint is only the endpoint-valued subclass, and its same value and procedure transfer through an endpoint-prior lower bound and a uniform upper-bound sandwich.

Within superpopulation stratified designs treating half of every stratum, matched pairs formed by the prognostic index minimize the mean-squared error of difference in means; that problem and the present fixed-population latent-discordance design class are non-nested.

For a fixed stratified design and a stated bounded group-CATE model, Theorem 2.1 optimizes a linear combination of observed group estimators; that fixed-design linear-estimator problem and the present joint design--all-estimator problem are non-nested.
The Gram--Schmidt Walk design controls a covariance-based balance--robustness trade-off and yields MSE and asymptotic inference guarantees for Horvitz--Thompson estimation.
Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population totals, the minimax bound is attained if and only if inclusion indicators are pairwise independent.
Under within-pair coin flips, the worst compatible binary attributable-effect allocation is a single boundary corner and exact inversion needs logarithmically many binomial tails.
Exact binary ATE intervals under balanced Bernoulli or matched-pair assignment can be computed with \(O(\log n)\) randomization tests.
Exact conservative stratified binary ATE inference can be obtained by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over compatible potential-outcome tables.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Hull's bounded-interval class is not identical to the present binary endpoint class, and the Bai and de Chaisemartin problems are non-nested comparators. The replacement records the precise transfer and removes the overstated equivalence.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For each path with \(s_J/J\to\rho\ge1/2\), prove a matching second-order liminf and recovery theorem for the profiled residual risks and then show that the minimizer contact set is necessary and sufficient for weak limits of exact finite minimizers.
open_obligations.obstruction: The established first-order game is flat on \(\mathcal F_\rho\). The exact finite conic certificates compute each fixed-\(J\) face but do not yield uniform second-order expansions. At \(\rho=1/2\), the hard-budget correction and unrestricted Airy correction compete only when \(\kappa_J=(s_J-J/2)/J^{2/3}\) is finite; the current core has neither the local pair-orbit kernel nor a matching lower expansion needed to promote the candidate upper-bound term into an epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit.
open_obligations.attempted: The scalar and two-parameter shrinking-prior experiments, including singular boundary information, give the sharp first-order value and envelope. Expanding those information bounds does not distinguish measures sharing the balance and mean-mixed constraints. Exact enumeration at \(J=2,3,4\) shows changing critical contact patterns and therefore cannot certify a stable exact-minimizer selection rule.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The exact finite contact system in Theorem 1 makes every set \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s_J)\) computable, and Theorem 5 proves
\[
 \mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\subseteq\mathcal F_\rho.
\]
Theorem 5 also recovers every \(\mu\in\mathcal F_\rho\) by invariant procedures whose excess worst risk is \(o(J^{-1})\).  At the critical boundary, writing \(\bar m_J=\int m\,d\mu_{q_J}\), the proposed hard-budget correction obeys the exact rescaling identity
\[
 J^{4/3}\frac{(2\bar m_J-1)(s_J-J/2)}{J^2}
 =\kappa_J(2\bar m_J-1).
\]
Thus finite \(\kappa_J\) is the only scale on which that correction and a \(J^{-4/3}\) unrestricted Airy correction can compete.  This calculation isolates the candidate penalty but does not prove its matching lower expansion, epi- or \(\Gamma\)-convergence, or replacement of first-order-optimal procedures by exact finite minimizers.

prose_updates.tldr: Known pairs are useful when their two units would respond similarly under each arm, but that two-arm similarity is latent. The integer \(s\) is therefore an analyst-specified sensitivity bound, and for every value the project jointly optimizes over all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable clipped SATE estimators. A pair-preserving symmetry reduction gives an exact finite conic game and dual certificate for the invariant optimal-design correspondence; a rational \(J=2,s=1\) instance rules out every paired--Bernoulli mixture. The sensitivity frontier satisfies \(J R^*(J,s_J)\to\min\{\rho,1/2\}\), while at and above the threshold the leading term leaves a measure-valued face. Exact selection on that face remains open. At \(\rho=1/2\), the concrete residual problem uses \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\), \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\), and the scale \(J^{4/3}\{R_J-1/(2J)\}\); the candidate hard-budget term is upper-bound evidence, not an established epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit.

project_justification.gap: SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 solves the unrestricted binary fixed-population experiment, while Hull2026BoundedOutcomes solves an unrestricted bounded-interval problem whose endpoint-valued schedules contain the present binary endpoint as a strict subclass. Hull's value and procedure transfer only through an endpoint least-favourable-prior lower bound and a uniform upper-bound sandwich, not by class identity. Bai2022MatchedPairs studies a superpopulation stratified half-treatment criterion, and deChaisemartin2022Shrinkage studies linear estimation under a fixed stratified design; both are non-nested with the present joint fixed-population design--estimator problem. None characterizes exact-minimizer limits on the measure-valued first-order face under a latent armwise discordance budget.
project_justification.niche: The sensitivity restriction breaks full unit exchangeability without treating unobserved potential-outcome discordance as pretreatment information. It leaves a finite but nontransitive observation experiment in which correlated assignment laws and nonlinear posterior-mean estimators can be jointly optimal.
project_justification.fill: For each selected \(s\), the project supplies the normalized assignment-marked orbit game, a matching least-favourable-prior dual, exact canonicality and uniqueness certificates, a strict noncanonical separation, a monotone risk sensitivity frontier, a first-order measure face, and exact randomization-test inversion. It isolates rather than claims the unresolved second-order selection theorem: at the critical boundary the candidate residual is an unrestricted Airy/local-experiment functional plus \(\kappa(2\int m\,d\mu-1)\), pending a matching lower expansion and exact-minimizer recovery.

prose_updates.related_work: Bai2023WhyRandomize supplies a symmetry template for group averaging, and Kallus2021Optimality shows that structured minimax design may require mixed assignment strategies under a difference-in-means precision criterion. At \(s=J\), \(\Theta_{J,J}\) is exactly the unrestricted binary schedule class of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026, so Proposition 2 is an exact reduction to that experiment. By contrast, \(\Theta_{J,J}\) is only the endpoint-valued subclass of Hull2026BoundedOutcomes's bounded-interval class. Hull's common minimax value and Bernoulli/nonlinear procedure transfer to the binary subclass by sandwiching: the endpoint-supported least-favourable prior supplies the lower bound, while Hull's uniform bounded-class risk bound supplies the upper bound. No class identity or experiment equivalence is asserted. Bai2022MatchedPairs considers a superpopulation stratified half-treatment problem, whereas deChaisemartin2022Shrinkage fixes the stratified design and optimizes within a linear estimator class. Those two problems are non-nested with the present fixed-array problem, which jointly optimizes every ex ante assignment law and every measurable clipped estimator under latent armwise pair discordance. HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 and AronowLopatto2026 inform balance and design-unbiasedness comparisons, and Wilson2026MatchedBinary, Zhang2026FastBinaryCI, and LiSpertusStark2025 inform exact inversion. The Airy expansion in SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 motivates the \(J^{-4/3}\) residual scale but does not supply a measure-valued pair-orbit epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact orbit kernel and conic contact system are finite and computable for every \(J\), and the rational \(J=2,s=1\) certificate proves strict noncanonicality. Numerical enumeration for \(J=2,3,4\) is only an early-kill check: critical grids have materially different coordinate ranges and do not determine a limiting exact-minimizer face. The second-order bookkeeping now isolates \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\). If a design correction is \((2\bar m_J-1)\Delta_J/J^2\), multiplying by \(J^{4/3}\) gives \(\kappa_J(2\bar m_J-1)\), exactly the scale of the unrestricted Airy correction. This is candidate upper-bound evidence only. No matching lower expansion, equicoercivity theorem, or exact-minimizer recovery has been proved. Finite \(\kappa\), \(\kappa=+\infty\), \(\kappa=-\infty\), and \(\rho>1/2\) require separate analyses. The van Trees applications in Theorems 4 and 5 use smooth boundary-vanishing priors and positive finite-cell experiments, so the tightened score, differentiation, boundary-flux, and positive-definiteness conditions remain satisfied.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The parameter \(s\) is an analyst-selected sensitivity index for latent both-arm discordance, not a quantity learned from observed outcomes. Every risk, optimal face, asymptotic regime, and confidence set is conditional on the selected value or sequence. At \(s=0\), paired assignment yields exact recovery. At \(s=J\), the schedule class is exactly the unrestricted binary class of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026. It is not Hull2026BoundedOutcomes's full bounded-interval class; only the same value and procedure transfer by the endpoint-prior/uniform-upper-bound sandwich. The exact finite orbit representation, endpoint reductions, rational noncanonical separation, first-order value, low-sensitivity concentration, high-sensitivity first-order envelope, and exact inversion are theorem obligations. The complete limit set of exact finite minimizers for \(\rho\ge1/2\) remains open, and the stated Airy-plus-budget functional is not claimed as a proved epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit.

proofs.proof_tex:
By \texttt{def:bounded-mismatch-class}, the inequalities \(D_a(Y)\le s\le s'\) imply
\[
 \Theta_{J,s}\subseteq\Theta_{J,s'}.
\]
The design and estimator classes are otherwise unchanged, so taking a supremum over the larger schedule class and then the same infimum gives \(R^*(J,s)\le R^*(J,s')\).

Suppose first that \(s=0\). Then each pair is homogeneous in each arm. Under \(q^{\mathrm{pair}}\), define the observable estimator
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{pair}}
 =\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J\sum_{r=1}^2
 \{A_{jr}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr}-(1-A_{jr})Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr}\}.
\]
Exactly one unit per pair is treated, and homogeneity makes the treated observation equal the pair's common treatment potential outcome and the control observation equal its common control potential outcome. Therefore \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{pair}}=\tau(Y)\) for every \(Y\in\Theta_{J,0}\), so nonnegativity of squared loss gives \(R^*(J,0)=0\).

For uniqueness among invariant orbit laws, suppose \(q_n>0\) for an orbit \(n\ne(0,0,J)\). Every assignment in that orbit has an unmixed pair. Fix one such assignment \(a\) and pair \(j\). If pair \(j\) is all control, take two schedules in \(\Theta_{J,0}\) that are zero everywhere except that the second schedule has both treatment potential outcomes in pair \(j\) equal to one. They give identical observations under \(a\), but their SATEs differ by \(1/J\). If pair \(j\) is all treated, make the analogous change to its two control potential outcomes. A single estimator value cannot equal both targets. Since the invariant law assigns probability \(q_n/C_n>0\) to \(a\), at least one of the two schedules has positive risk. Thus zero worst-case risk forces support only on \((0,0,J)\), proving \(\mathcal Q^*(J,0)=\{q^{\mathrm{pair}}\}\).

At \(s=J\), both discordance inequalities are vacuous, hence
\[
 \Theta_{J,J}=\{0,1\}^{\mathcal P_J\times\{0,1\}},
 \qquad R^*(J,J)=r^{\mathrm U}_{2J}
\]
by the two minimax definitions. The cited unrestricted binary theorem states that independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment and its nonlinear least-favourable-prior Bayes rule attain this value. Its orbit masses are \(C_n/4^J=q_n^{\mathrm{Ber}}\). The invariant reduction of Theorem 1 therefore places \(q^{\mathrm{Ber}}\) in \(\mathcal Q^*(J,J)\), with the asserted posterior-mean estimator.
